chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from 'Asim al-Khayyat, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites Surah al-Nahl every month would be spared from debt in the world and from seventy types of calamities, the least of which are insanity, leprosy, and white spots, and his dwelling would be in Jannat al-Adn, which is the middle of the Gardens.

key_terms.الْجِنَانِ: The Gardens (plural of Jannah, referring to Paradise)
key_terms.جَنَّهِ عَدْنٍ: Jannat al-Adn (Garden of Eden/Abode of Permanence)
key_terms.سُورَهَ النَّحْلِ: Surah al-Nahl (The Bee), the 16th chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of reciting Surah al-Nahl every month according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the spiritual and physical protection granted through the monthly recitation of Surah al-Nahl, linking it to the removal of both material debts and seventy specific calamities, with insanity being the least severe. The promise of dwelling in Jannat al-Adn, identified as the central realm of Paradise, underscores the high status of this Surah in Shia devotional practice as a means of securing divine favor and ultimate salvation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from ’Asim al-Khayyat from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “

One who recites Surah Nahl every month would not see harm in the world and would be immune from seventy diseases the least of whom are insanity, leprosy and white spots. And his destination would be Jannat-e-Adn inside Paradise.”
